close_reason: Fixed in commit 0decea2d. pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs from_pem/from_der/from_der_iter now decode via TrustAnchor::try_from rather than TrustAnchor::from_cert. Malformed NameConstraints now surface as Error::Der (from_pem, from_der) or Error::MalformedAnchor(i) (from_der_iter). 8 new integration tests in tests/malformed_nc.rs with pyca/cryptography-generated fixtures (.der and .pem) committed in tests/fixtures/. Workspace tests + clippy --all-features -D warnings + rustdoc --no-deps -D warnings + cargo doc all clean for pkix-truststore. Independent oracle: pyca x509.UnrecognizedExtension(NC_OID, b'\\xff\\xfe\\x00\\x01') marked critical=True — known-garbage DER for the NC SEQUENCE.
description:
pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs:334,351,378 all use TrustAnchor::from_cert, which the pkix-path rustdoc (pkix-path/src/lib.rs:696-704) explicitly documents as silently dropping malformed NameConstraints extensions and continuing.

Trigger: a trust anchor with a NameConstraints extension whose DER is unparseable (truncated, wrong tag class, malformed GeneralSubtrees) is loaded by from_pem / from_der / from_der_iter.

Actual behavior: the anchor is accepted with name_constraints = None. The anchor will NOT enforce its NameConstraints at validation time. RFC 5280 §4.2 requires a relying party to reject a certificate with an unrecognised critical extension; the constraint here is that you cannot enforce a constraint you could not parse.

Severity: for a *trust anchor* this is a fail-open: the deployment author asserted 'this root may only sign for *.example.com' via NameConstraints, the anchor file is corrupted, pkix-truststore loads it anyway, and the validator now trusts that root for any name.

Fix options:
 a) Use TrustAnchor::try_from(cert) and propagate Error::Der (the safer default; the strict-mode contract pkix-path already documents).
 b) Add a 'strict' loader variant alongside the lenient one and document each.
 c) Surface a per-anchor warning channel.

Option (a) is the right default for a Tier-1 trust-store loader. Trust anchors are not bulk subscriber certs; loading a few hundred at startup with a strict policy is fine. The current behavior re-exports a fail-open semantics through a function that does not signal it.
title: TrustAnchor::from_cert silently swallows malformed NameConstraints on every loaded anchor
